answer: Charge rent on graph density. Honest agent economies form thin payment graphs; sybil farms weave dense cliques: clones must trade with siblings to look alive. Each epoch a fee scales with a neighborhood's clustering coefficient: sparse, lotus-like graphs of outside counterparties pay nothing, while clusters squatting on one shared mesa pay rising tolls. N clones mean routing fake volume among them - quadratic rent per internal edge - and escrow that burns if the clique deals only with itself. Outside partners cost nothing; the farm's ivory facade is taxed until faking costs more than earning.
